characters.name: Macbeth
characters.role: General of the King's army; Thane of Glamis/Cawdor; King of Scotland

key_speeches.line: Methought I heard a voice cry 'Sleep no more! Macbeth does murder sleep'
Avaunt! and quit my sight! let the earth hide thee!
key_speeches.context: Seeing the ghost of Banquo at the banquet.

key_speeches.line: Come, you spirits That tend on mortal thoughts, unsex me here, And fill me from the crown to the toe top-full Of direst cruelty!
key_speeches.context: Invoking spirits to remove her femininity and compassion.

key_speeches.line: My hands are of your colour; but I shame To wear a heart so white.
key_speeches.context: Rebuking Macbeth for his guilt after the murder.

key_speeches.line: Sit, worthy friends: my lord is often thus, And hath been from his youth:
key_speeches.context: Trying to cover for Macbeth's erratic behavior at the banquet.

characters.name: Banquo
characters.role: General of the King's army; Macbeth's friend

key_speeches.line: Were such things here as we do speak about? Or have we eaten on the insane root That takes the reason prisoner?
key_speeches.context: Questioning the reality of the witches' appearance.

key_speeches.line: I have begun to plant thee, and will labour To make thee full of growing.
key_speeches.context: Rewarding Macbeth with the title Thane of Cawdor.

key_speeches.line: This castle hath a pleasant seat; the air Nimbly and sweetly recommends itself Unto our gentle senses.
Who can be wise, amazed, temperate and furious, Loyal and neutral, in a moment? No man:
key_speeches.context: Reacting to the discovery of Duncan's murder.
Informing Macbeth that Macduff has fled.
Explaining how he will live after his father's death.
Questioning his mother about the definition of a traitor.
